name: bridge-tally
description: Ask about the TallyPrime books on this computer, and prepare Journal, Payment, Receipt and Contra vouchers as a local file. Posting is off until you turn it on below; then it posts one voucher at a time, each after you approve it in a native dialog. What it reads, amounts included, goes to your AI provider; Response redaction can only shorten party and ledger names and bank account numbers or drop narrations.

redaction.title: Response redaction
redaction.description: What to hide from your AI provider: none, mask_parties (shortens party and ledger names and bank account numbers to their first two and last two characters) or drop_narration (removes narrations). Neither hides amounts, company names, PAN, GSTIN, IFSC, MSME or Udyam registration numbers, contact details or references. Any other value stops the connector from starting.

enable_writes.title: Allow voucher posting (Journal, Payment, Receipt, Contra)
enable_writes.description: Off by default. When on, ComplyEaze Bridge can post one Journal, Payment, Receipt or Contra into Tally at a time, each only after you approve it in a separate window. Leave it off unless you accept the known limits in Terms of Use section 9.2 (Posting), including these four: 1) Tally picks the company by name. A company renamed to, or opened under, that name (or one differing only in capitals or spaces) right after the last check could still receive the voucher. ComplyEaze Bridge may flag it afterwards, but cannot always say where the voucher went, and cannot prevent it. 2) A ledger renamed and replaced in that same moment can receive the post instead. It is marked for checking when seen, but not every such change is seen. 3) There is no undo: a wrong post must be corrected by hand in Tally. 4) The approval window covers only ComplyEaze Bridge: another Tally connector in the same Claude Desktop that can change entries can do so without it. You can also record, in another window, that you reviewed a voucher marked for checking; that writes nothing to Tally. Reading, bank-statement parsing and voucher file preparation work either way.
